masked: Shown as qualified / not qualified only
securityMasked: Security qualification: Kafa'a mirrors qualified or not qualified only. Tasks, dates and evaluators stay in ENEC's security systems.
requalNote: Requalification every {n} months. Notices go out 90, 60 and 30 days before expiry unless the standard sets other intervals.

mirror.title: A mirror, not the record
mirror.body: Until ENEC approves Kafa'a as the system of record, these cards mirror ENEC's training records system. Kafa'a never sets a qualification status by itself: changes come from evaluations signed by a qualified evaluator, or from the source system.

eval.title: Task evaluation
eval.criticalHint: A failed critical step fails the task whatever else went well.
eval.criticalNote: This is a critical task: a failed critical step fails the evaluation.
eval.correctHint: Records are append-only: a correction adds a new entry that supersedes the earlier one.
eval.confirmBody: You are recording {result} on {task} for {person}. This cannot be edited later; a correction would be a new entry.
eval.selfBody: An evaluator cannot sign off their own qualification. The request will be refused and logged.
eval.notEvaluatorTitle: You do not hold the evaluator qualification for this standard
eval.notEvaluatorBody: You can view records, but sign-offs will be refused until your evaluator qualification for this standard is current.

gap.none: No required standards recorded for this role

lib.intro: What "competent" means for nuclear roles at Barakah: 14 domains, four levels, and the roles that need each competency.
lib.layer1Body: Proficiency levels describe how far someone has developed in a domain. They guide development plans and career moves. They do not authorise anyone to do safety-related work.
lib.layer2Body: Qualification cards record who is qualified to do which task, with an evaluator's sign-off and an expiry. This is what authorises work. Staff see their own cards under My qualifications.
lib.satTitle: Built on the Systematic Approach to Training
lib.satBody: Job and task analysis produces task lists; task lists produce qualification cards; cards are completed through on-the-job training and task performance evaluations, including job performance measures (JPMs).
lib.compsDesc: {n} competencies in {d} domains. Open one for its level descriptors and the roles that need it.
lib.heatTitle: Highest level required, by domain and job family
lib.heatDesc: Each cell shows the highest proficiency level any role in the family needs in the domain (empty = not required).

verify.intro: Check a Kafa'a-issued course certificate by its number. Only internal courses issue these certificates.
verify.notFanrTitle: This is not an operator licence check
verify.notFanrBody: Kafa'a never verifies FANR operator certificates. Operator certification is recorded by FANR.
verify.note: Internal Kafa'a course certificate. Not an operator licence.
verify.notFoundBody: We could not find {no}. Check the number on the certificate and try again.
verify.format: Use letters, digits and hyphens only (6 to 32 characters).

my.intro: Your qualification cards, task by task: status, evaluator role, date and expiry.
my.noneBody: Cards appear here when you start a qualification standard for your role.
my.gapTarget: Standards for a role I want
my.pickTarget: Choose a role to see which of its qualification standards you already hold.
my.openPlanner: Plan the path to this role

team.intro: Qualification readiness for the people in your scope, with expiries, acknowledgements and notices.
team.noTeam: No one in your scope yet
team.noTeamBody: Your scope is set by your role assignment (for example a crew or a team).
team.noticesBody: Notices go to each person and their manager 90, 60 and 30 days before a qualification expires (or at the standard's own intervals). Items within 30 days show as due in the matrix.
team.sweepConsequence: Kafa'a checks every record in your scope, sends any notices not already sent, marks records due within 30 days, and marks past-dated records expired.
team.calendarDesc: Qualifications expiring in the next {n} days.
team.acksDesc: Sign-off flow: trainee, qualified evaluator, then supervisor acknowledgement.
team.ackConsequence: You confirm, as supervisor, the evaluation of {task} for {person}. You cannot acknowledge an evaluation you performed.

crew.title: Crew licences
crew.desc: Certificate validity and this quarter's shift proficiency for your crew.
crew.note: Shift supervisors see validity and proficiency for their crew only, and availability as available or not available. No medical detail is shown.
crew.none: No licensed operators in your scope

matrix.intro: People in your scope against qualification standards, coloured by status. Due means within 30 days of expiry.
matrix.tabWho: Who is qualified for task X
matrix.footnote: * needs review after a standard revision. Security qualifications show qualified or not qualified only. Select a person for their cards and gap analysis.

who.desc: For work planners: people in your scope who currently hold the qualification and have passed the task.
who.none: No one in your scope is qualified for this task
who.noneBody: Check another task, or ask the training team about upcoming evaluations.
who.scopeNote: Limited to people in your scope

stds.intro: Qualification standards (versioned qualification cards) with task lists, JPMs, requalification intervals and the records that depend on them.
stds.title: Title
stds.noEvaluator: You do not hold an evaluator qualification.
stds.queueEmpty: Nothing waiting on standards you evaluate.

std.revisedBody: {n} records were flagged for review. Decide each one in the review tab: carry it over or require retraining.
std.restrictedBody: Security training content stays in ENEC's security systems. Kafa'a shows qualified or not qualified only.
std.satBody: Trainee completes on-the-job training; a qualified evaluator signs each task (JPMs where listed); the supervisor acknowledges. Records are append-only: corrections create a new entry with a reason.
std.noRecordsBody: Records appear for people in your scope who hold or are working on this standard.
std.recordOnOtherVersion: This record is on version {v}. Review it to move it to the current version before evaluating.
std.noReviewBody: Records are flagged here when a revision changes this standard.
std.reviewBody: A change to the task list or procedure may affect these people. Carry a record over when the change does not affect them, or require retraining.
std.reviewConsequence: The record moves to the current version of the standard. Retraining sets it to in progress until the changed tasks are evaluated again.
std.impactBody: {n} records on this version will be flagged for review.
std.reasonHint: For example: procedure revision after a modification or an operating-experience lesson.
std.taskEdits: Task list for the new version

reasons.ins_fit: Has {have} of the {need} skills this standard covers at level 2 or above
reasons.ins_sme_profile: Has a subject-matter expert profile in the knowledge capture studio

ins.mirrorBody: Kafa'a mirrors the licensee's instructor qualification records to plan the pipeline. It issues no FANR status: qualification decisions stay with the licensee's training organisation. The currency rule (40 delivery hours and 8 hours of continuing development a year) is a SAMPLE demo setting.

currency.title: Annual currency
currency.lapsedOn: Currency lapsed on {date}: the 12-month window ended under the minimum.
currency.rule: Currency lapses when the hours in a 12-month window fall below the minimum; notices go out 90, 60 and 30 days before the review date.

req.accepted: Nomination accepted by the training manager
req.initialWait: Assigned on acceptance; completion comes from the training records system
req.coTeach: Two co-teach observations passed, by two different observers
req.solo: One solo observed delivery passed, by a third observer
req.qualifiedWait: The training manager confirms; an observer of the set cannot

form.title: Record an observation
form.rule: Pass needs 75% or more and no critical item rated "not met". You cannot observe yourself; qualification needs three different observers.
form.confirmBody: {kind}: {score}%, {result}. Observations are append-only; a correction is a new observation.

hours.logBody: Records delivery or development hours for this instructor (mirror of the scheduling system).
hours.logBodySelf: Records your own continuing development hours.

nominate.title: Nominate {name} for the instructor track
nominate.body: The training manager decides the nomination. On acceptance the instructor initial training course is assigned.
nominate.motivation: Why this person (or you) should teach
nominate.securityNote: Security standards and security, cyber and safeguards roles are career-path only and never join the track.

facts.title: Programme facts
facts.asipBody: Barakah foundation training includes the Accelerated SRO Instructor Program and the Instructor Initial and Continuing Training Qualification (per source).
facts.asipSrc: UAE National Report, 10th CNS Review Meeting (March 2026), Art. 11, p. 75
facts.reg16Body: FANR-REG-16 Art. 9 requires systematic, performance-based training delivered by qualified instructors, including for contractors.
facts.fanr65Body: FANR's own Internal Trainer Qualification Programme certifies 65 subject-matter experts to deliver technical and non-technical training (the regulator's programme, per source).
facts.fanr65Src: UAE National Report, 10th CNS Review Meeting (March 2026), Art. 8, p. 40

board.intro: The pool of qualified instructors with their annual currency, the pipeline from SME nomination to qualification, the observation queue and the teaching hours log.
board.statPipelineSub: {ready} ready to qualify · {nominated} nominations to decide
board.statHours: Delivery hours in the current windows
board.sweepBody: Instructors whose 12-month window ended under the minimum lapse on that date and their evaluator rows end; the others are renewed; 90, 60 and 30-day notices go to instructors short of hours.
board.syncBody: Delivered M04 sessions with at least one attendee marked present are added once to the instructor's hours log.
board.poolCaption: Qualified instructors and their annual currency
board.queueEmpty: No candidate is waiting for an observation
board.queueIntro: Candidates waiting for a co-teach or solo observation. You cannot observe your own track; the qualifying set needs three different observers.

act.youObserved: You observed this candidate: another training manager may need to qualify them
act.acceptBody: The instructor initial training course is assigned and the candidate is told to start.
act.declineBody: The candidate sees your reason and can volunteer again later.
act.qualifyBody: Records the qualification (maker-checker), starts the annual currency, writes evaluator rows for the standards and adds the instructing skill to the person's skills profile.
act.reinstateBody: A passed currency observation after the lapse restarts the annual currency and the evaluator rows.
act.withdrawBody: The track closes; a qualified instructor's evaluator rows end today.

find.none: No colleague in your view matches this standard yet

track.notFound: This instructor track is not in your view
track.intro: Stages, observed deliveries, annual currency and teaching hours for one instructor.
track.ownNote: This is your own track: you cannot observe or qualify yourself.
track.makerBody: You observed part of this candidate's qualifying set, and no complete set exists without you. Another training manager has to decide.
track.observationsIntro: Checklist of observable behaviours tied to the course objectives (the F25 level-3 mechanics). Critical items must not be "not met".
track.evaluatorNone: None yet: they are written when the instructor qualifies
track.evaluatorNote: Written by the qualification and kept in step with the currency; they end when the currency lapses or the track closes.

my.intro: Teach what you know: from SME nomination to qualified instructor, with your observed deliveries and annual currency in one place.

next.nominated: The training manager is reviewing your nomination.
next.initial_training: Complete the instructor initial training course ({code}). It is in My learning.
next.co_teach: Co-teach two sessions with two different instructors observing you.
next.solo: Deliver one session on your own, observed by a third instructor.
next.ready: All observations are complete: the training manager will confirm your qualification.
next.lapsed: Your currency lapsed. A passed currency observation lets the training manager reinstate you.
next.currencyShort: Before {date} you still need {hours} delivery hours and {cpd} development hours.
next.currencyOk: Your currency for this year is met. Keep teaching and logging your development.

my.how1: Volunteer, or be nominated by your line manager or the training manager.
my.how2: The training manager accepts and assigns {code}.
my.how3: Co-teach twice, observed by two different instructors.
my.how4: Deliver solo, observed by a third instructor.
my.how5: The training manager qualifies you; keep 40 delivery and 8 development hours a year.
my.withdrawBody: Your track closes. You can volunteer again later.
my.teachBody: Your skills profile suggests standards you could teach. Volunteer and the training manager will review it.
my.notStaff: The instructor track is open to ENEC staff.
my.noMatch: No standard matches your skills profile at level 2 yet. You can still volunteer.

team.intro: Find subject-matter experts in your team and nominate them; follow their progress on the instructor track.
team.tracks: My team on the instructor track
team.tracksIntro: Tracks of people in your scope.
team.noTracks: Nobody in your team is on the instructor track yet
team.findIntro: Ranked from the skills profile, SME profiles and SME mentor nominations. No personal attributes are used.
team.how: Your nomination goes to the training manager. Accepted candidates take the instructor initial training, co-teach twice and deliver solo before they qualify.
